explain.es:
En el mapa de ESTILO INDIRECTO aprendiste a contar afirmaciones. Aquí vamos a contar preguntas, órdenes, peticiones y consejos. El paso atrás de tiempos, pronombres y expresiones de tiempo sigue igual, pero hay tres novedades:
• las preguntas indirectas llevan orden de frase afirmativa (sin inversión, sin do / does / did y sin ?);
• las órdenes y peticiones van con to + infinitivo;
• en lugar de say o tell, usamos reporting verbs más precisos (advise, refuse, suggest…).
explain.en: Reported questions use statement word order; commands and requests use (not) to + infinitive; reporting verbs summarise what people meant.

explain.title: Truco: la pregunta desinflada
explain.es: Piensa que la pregunta indirecta es una pregunta desinflada: pierde el aire (do, does, did), pierde la forma (la inversión) y pierde el gorrito (?). Y para órdenes y peticiones, recuerda: TO = TOdo lo que alguien te pide u ordena (told me to, asked me to).
explain.en: A reported question loses do / does / did, the inversion and the question mark. Commands and requests → to.

explain.title: 1 · Preguntas con Wh-
explain.es: Repetimos la palabra interrogativa (what, where, when, why, how, who…) y después ponemos sujeto + verbo, como en una frase normal. Desaparecen do / does / did y el signo de interrogación, y el verbo da el paso atrás. Para introducirlas usamos ask (+ persona), want to know o wonder.
explain.en: Keep the question word, then subject + verb. No do / does / did, no question mark, and backshift the tense.

examples.en: “Where do you work?” → She asked me where I worked.
“What time does the film start?” → He asked what time the film started.
examples.es: «¿A qué hora empieza la peli?» → Preguntó a qué hora empezaba la peli.

examples.en: “Why are you crying?” → My dad asked me why I was crying.
examples.es: «¿Por qué lloras?» → Mi padre me preguntó por qué lloraba.

explain.title: 2 · Preguntas de sí / no: if o whether
explain.es: Si la pregunta no tiene palabra interrogativa (se contesta con yes / no), añadimos if o whether (= si) y después sujeto + verbo. Whether es un poco más formal y es el preferido con or not: She asked whether or not I was coming. ¡Ojo! Este if no es el del condicional: aquí significa si en el sentido de whether.
explain.en: For yes / no questions, add if or whether + subject + verb. Whether is slightly more formal.

examples.en: “Are you hungry?” → She asked me if I was hungry.
examples.es: «¿Tienes hambre?» → Me preguntó si tenía hambre.

examples.en: “Did you lock the door?” → He wanted to know whether I had locked the door.
examples.es: «¿Cerraste con llave?» → Quería saber si había cerrado con llave.

examples.en: “Can I pay by card?” → The customer asked if she could pay by card.
examples.es: «¿Puedo pagar con tarjeta?» → La clienta preguntó si podía pagar con tarjeta.

explain.title: Pregunta directa o indirecta
explain.es: La gran diferencia es el orden de las palabras. En español apenas cambia (¿Dónde vive? → Preguntó dónde vivía), por eso los hispanohablantes arrastramos la inversión. En inglés, la pregunta indirecta ya no es una pregunta: es una afirmación y termina en punto.
explain.en: A reported question is not a question any more: statement word order and a full stop.

cols.head: 📝 Indirecta · Reported
items: They asked if I had enjoyed it.

explain.title: 3 · Preguntas de sujeto
explain.es: Cuando who o what es el sujeto de la pregunta, la pregunta directa ya no tiene inversión (Who called?), así que en indirecto el orden es el mismo: solo hay que dar el paso atrás. ¡No metas un sujeto extra!
explain.en: If who / what is the subject, the word order stays the same: just backshift the verb.

examples.es: «¿Quién ha llamado?» → Preguntó quién había llamado.

examples.en: “What happened?” → The police officer asked what had happened.
examples.es: «¿Qué ha pasado?» → El policía preguntó qué había pasado.

examples.en: “Who wants more cake?” → Grandma asked who wanted more cake.
examples.es: «¿Quién quiere más tarta?» → La abuela preguntó quién quería más tarta.

explain.title: 4 · Órdenes: tell + persona + (not) to
explain.es: Para contar una orden o una instrucción usamos tell + persona + to + infinitivo. Si la orden es negativa, not va delante de to. En español usamos el subjuntivo (me dijo que me sentara), pero en inglés nunca se dice told me that I sit. Mismo patrón: order, instruct, remind, warn.
explain.en: Commands: tell + person + (not) to + infinitive. Not goes before to.

examples.en: “Sit down, please.” → The teacher told us to sit down.
examples.es: «Sentaos, por favor». → El profesor nos dijo que nos sentáramos.

examples.en: “Don't use your phone.” → My boss told me not to use my phone.
examples.es: «No uses el móvil». → Mi jefe me dijo que no usara el móvil.

examples.en: “Remember to buy milk.” → Mum reminded me to buy milk.
examples.es: «Acuérdate de comprar leche». → Mamá me recordó que comprara leche.

explain.title: 5 · Peticiones: ask + persona + (not) to
explain.es: Las peticiones (Can you…? Could you…? Would you mind…? …, please) se cuentan con ask + persona + (not) to + infinitivo. Aunque la frase directa tenga forma de pregunta, en indirecto ya no es una pregunta: es un favor que alguien pidió. Compara: She asked me if I could swim (pregunta sobre capacidad) / She asked me to swim (petición).
explain.en: Requests: ask + person + (not) to + infinitive, even if the original was a question.

examples.en: “Can you send me the file?” → My colleague asked me to send him the file.
examples.es: «¿Me mandas el archivo?» → Mi compañero me pidió que le mandara el archivo.

examples.en: “Could you not make so much noise?” → Our neighbour asked us not to make so much noise.
examples.es: «¿Podríais no hacer tanto ruido?» → El vecino nos pidió que no hiciéramos tanto ruido.

examples.en: “Please call me back.” → She asked me to call her back.
examples.es: «Llámame, por favor». → Me pidió que la llamara.

explain.title: Resumen: preguntas, órdenes y peticiones
head: Tipo · Type
Directo · Direct
Indirecto · Reported
Clave · Key
rows: The teacher asked who had broken the window.
He told me to close the door.
She told us not to touch it.
He asked me to open the window.
explain.note: En órdenes y peticiones no hay paso atrás: el infinitivo con to no tiene tiempo. Lo que sí cambian son los pronombres y las expresiones de tiempo.
explain.note_en: No backshift with to + infinitive; pronouns and time words still change.

explain.title: Reporting verbs: los patrones
head: Patrón · Pattern
Verbos · Verbs
Directo · Direct
Indirecto · Reported
rows: advise, ask, encourage, invite, order, persuade, remind, tell, warn
apologise for, insist on, complain about
accuse sb of, blame sb for, congratulate sb on, thank sb for
She accused him of stealing her idea.
admit, agree, complain, explain, promise, suggest
He explained that the printer was broken.
explain.note: Los reporting verbs resumen la intención del hablante, así que no hace falta copiar todas sus palabras: “OK, OK, I'll do it.” → He agreed to do it.
explain.note_en: Reporting verbs summarise the speaker's intention.

warn sb (not) to
remind sb to
invite sb to
offer to
refuse to
promise to
agree to
threaten to
suggest + -ing

apologise for
insist on

explain.title: 6 · SUGGEST, el verbo trampa
explain.es: Suggest es el reporting verb que más falla a los hispanohablantes, porque en español decimos me sugirió que fuera. En inglés nunca va con persona + to: He suggested me to go. Hay dos opciones: suggest + -ing (sobre todo cuando incluye al que habla) o suggest (that) + sujeto + (should) + infinitivo. Con recommend pasa algo parecido: recommend + -ing o recommend (that)…
explain.en: suggest + -ing / suggest (that) + subject + (should) + infinitive. Never suggest sb to.

examples.en: “Let's eat out tonight.” → Ana suggested eating out that night.
examples.es: «Cenemos fuera esta noche». → Ana propuso cenar fuera esa noche.

examples.en: “Why don't you take a break?” → He suggested (that) I (should) take a break.
examples.es: «¿Por qué no te tomas un descanso?» → Me sugirió que me tomara un descanso.

examples.en: “You should book early.” → The guide recommended booking early.
examples.es: «Deberíais reservar pronto». → El guía recomendó reservar pronto.

items.en: “Have you ever been to Japan?” → She asked me if I had ever been to Japan.
items.es: Me preguntó si había estado alguna vez en Japón.

items.en: “How long have you lived here?” → The new neighbour asked how long we had lived there.
items.es: La nueva vecina preguntó cuánto tiempo llevábamos viviendo allí.

items.en: “Where can I park?” → The driver wanted to know where he could park.
items.es: El conductor quería saber dónde podía aparcar.

items.en: “Is breakfast included?” → I asked whether breakfast was included.
items.es: Pregunté si el desayuno estaba incluido.

items.en: “What are you going to do after university?” → My grandad asked me what I was going to do after university.
items.es: Mi abuelo me preguntó qué iba a hacer después de la universidad.

items.en: “Fasten your seatbelts.” → The pilot told the passengers to fasten their seatbelts.
items.es: El piloto les dijo a los pasajeros que se abrocharan el cinturón.

items.en: “Please don't tell anyone.” → Lucía asked me not to tell anyone.
items.es: Lucía me pidió que no se lo contara a nadie.

items.en: “I'll help you with your CV.” → My sister offered to help me with my CV.
items.es: Mi hermana se ofreció a ayudarme con el currículum.

items.en: “No, I won't apologise!” → He refused to apologise.
“Don't touch the cables!” → The electrician warned us not to touch the cables.
items.es: El electricista nos advirtió que no tocáramos los cables.

items.en: “I didn't take the money.” → She denied taking the money.
“Congratulations on passing your exam!” → They congratulated me on passing my exam.
items.es: Me felicitaron por aprobar el examen.

items.bad: She asked me where did I live.
items.why: Pregunta indirecta = orden de afirmativa: sin did y sin inversión.

items.bad: He asked me what was my name.
items.good: He asked me what my name was.
items.why: Sujeto (my name) + verbo (was), como en una afirmación.

items.bad: She asked me if I was hungry?
items.good: She asked me if I was hungry.
items.why: Ya no es una pregunta: termina en punto.
items.why_en: Full stop, not a question mark.

items.bad: He asked me do I want a coffee.
items.good: He asked me if I wanted a coffee.
items.why: Sí / no → if / whether + sujeto + verbo (con paso atrás).
items.why_en: Yes / no → if / whether + subject + verb.

items.bad: She told me that I sit down.
items.why: Órdenes → tell + persona + to + infinitivo, no el subjuntivo del español.

items.bad: He told us to not shout.
My friend suggested me to take the train.
items.good: My friend suggested taking the train. / …suggested (that) I take the train.

items.why: Órdenes: tell / ask + persona + to. Say no lleva persona.
items.why_en: tell / ask sb to, not say sb to.

items.en: What is it: a question, a command, a request, advice…?

items.es: Wh- → asked (me) + wh- + sujeto + verbo. Sí / no → asked (me) + if / whether + sujeto + verbo.
items.en: Wh- → asked + wh- + subject + verb; yes / no → if / whether.

items.es: En preguntas: quita do / does / did, da el paso atrás y termina con punto.
items.en: Remove do / does / did, backshift, full stop.

items.es: Orden → told + persona + (not) to. Petición → asked + persona + (not) to.
items.en: Command → told sb (not) to; request → asked sb (not) to.

items.es: ¿Hay un verbo más preciso? → offered, refused, advised, suggested… con su patrón (to, sb + to, -ing).
items.en: Choose a precise reporting verb and its pattern.

items.es: Revisa pronombres y expresiones de tiempo (tomorrow → the next day).
items.en: Check pronouns and time words.

lines.en: How was the interview? What did they ask you?
First they asked me why I wanted to work for them.
lines.es: Primero me preguntaron por qué quería trabajar con ellos.

lines.en: Classic! Did they ask if you spoke other languages?
Yes, and they wanted to know whether I had ever lived abroad.
lines.es: Sí, y querían saber si había vivido alguna vez en el extranjero.

lines.en: The manager asked me to describe a difficult situation at work. Then she told me to wait outside for a few minutes.
lines.es: La jefa me pidió que describiera una situación difícil en el trabajo. Luego me dijo que esperara fuera unos minutos.

lines.en: It was! When I came back in, she offered to show me the office and invited me to come back on Monday.
lines.es: ¡Lo fue! Cuando volví a entrar, se ofreció a enseñarme la oficina y me invitó a volver el lunes.

exercises.es: Rodea la opción correcta. Piensa: ¿pregunta, orden o reporting verb?

items.q: She asked me where [I lived|did I live].
items.a: I lived

items.q: He asked [if|that] I was ready.
items.a: if

items.q: They wanted to know what time [the train left|did the train leave].
items.a: the train left

items.q: The teacher told us [to be|be] quiet.
items.a: to be

items.q: My mum told me [not to|to not] stay out late.
items.a: not to

items.q: I asked her [whether|what] she had enjoyed the concert.
items.a: whether

items.q: He asked me [to help|that I help] him with his luggage.
items.a: to help

items.q: She suggested [going|to go] to the cinema.
items.a: going

items.q: They asked us how long [we had been|had we been] waiting.
items.a: we had been

items.q: He refused [to answer|answering] the question.
items.a: to answer

exercises.title: Preguntas con Wh-
exercises.es: Pasa la pregunta a estilo indirecto. Empieza con las palabras dadas. ¡Sin inversión y sin interrogación!

items.q: “Where do you live?” → She asked me…
items.a: She asked me where I lived.

items.q: “What are you doing?” → He asked me…
items.a: He asked me what I was doing.

items.q: “Why did you leave your job?” → The interviewer asked me…
items.a: The interviewer asked me why I had left my job.

items.q: “How much does this jacket cost?” → I asked the shop assistant…
items.a: I asked the shop assistant how much that (the) jacket cost.

items.q: “When will the results be ready?” → The students wanted to know…
items.a: The students wanted to know when the results would be ready.

items.q: “Who has eaten my sandwich?” → Tom asked…
items.a: Tom asked who had eaten his sandwich.

items.q: “Where can we buy tickets?” → The tourists asked…
items.a: The tourists asked where they could buy tickets.

items.q: “How long have you been learning English?” → My new teacher asked me…
items.a: My new teacher asked me how long I had been learning English.

exercises.title: Preguntas de sí / no
exercises.es: Usa if o whether. Cambia tiempos, pronombres y expresiones de tiempo.

items.q: “Are you coming to the party?” → Laura asked me…
items.a: Laura asked me if (whether) I was coming to the party.

items.q: “Do you like sushi?” → He asked her…
items.a: He asked her if (whether) she liked sushi.

items.q: “Have you seen my keys?” → Dad asked us…
items.a: Dad asked us if (whether) we had seen his keys.

items.q: “Did you pass the exam?” → My aunt asked me…
items.a: My aunt asked me if (whether) I had passed the exam.

items.q: “Can I borrow your charger?” → Leo asked me…
items.a: Leo asked me if (whether) he could borrow my charger.

items.q: “Will you be at home tomorrow?” → The courier asked me…
items.a: The courier asked me if (whether) I would be at home the next (following) day.

exercises.title: Órdenes y peticiones
exercises.es: Usa told o asked + persona + (not) to + infinitivo.

items.q: “Turn off your phones,” the teacher said to us.
items.a: The teacher told us to turn off our phones.

items.q: “Don't be late,” my boss said to me.
items.a: My boss told me not to be late.

items.q: “Can you lend me ten euros?” Ana said to me.
items.a: Ana asked me to lend her ten euros.

items.q: “Please don't park here,” the man said to us.
items.a: The man asked us not to park there.

items.q: “Open your books at page 20,” the teacher said to the class.
items.a: The teacher told the class to open their books at page 20.

items.q: “Could you speak more slowly?” I said to the guide.
items.a: I asked the guide to speak more slowly.

items.q: “Don't touch anything!” the police officer said to the reporters.
items.a: The police officer told the reporters not to touch anything.

items.q: “Would you mind closing the window?” she said to me.
items.a: She asked me to close the window.

exercises.title: Ordena la frase
exercises.es: Ordena las palabras. Recuerda: las preguntas indirectas terminan en punto.

items.q: asked / she / where / me / lived / I
items.a: She asked me where I lived.

items.q: he / if / was / I / asked / ready
items.a: He asked if I was ready.

items.q: told / the / us / to / doctor / rest
items.a: The doctor told us to rest.

items.q: not / me / she / to / asked / worry
items.a: She asked me not to worry.

items.q: know / they / wanted / to / what / time / the / film / started
items.a: They wanted to know what time the film started.

items.q: whether / wondered / I / they / had / arrived / safely
items.a: I wondered whether they had arrived safely.

items.q: suggested / a / we / she / taxi / that / take
items.a: She suggested that we take a taxi.

items.q: apologised / he / late / for / being
items.a: He apologised for being late.

exercises.title: Lee y contesta
exercises.es: Lee el blog de Clara. Marca T (true) o F (false) y contesta las preguntas.
exercises.en: Read Clara's blog. Tick T or F and answer the questions.
text: When I landed in Toronto last summer, the officer at passport control was very serious. First, she asked me where I had flown from and how long I was planning to stay in Canada. I told her I was staying for three weeks.

Then she wanted to know whether I was travelling alone and if I had a return ticket. I said I was visiting my cousin. She asked me what my cousin did for a living, and I explained that he was a nurse in a hospital downtown.

Finally, she asked me to look at the camera and told me not to move. After a few seconds, she smiled, stamped my passport and told me to enjoy my stay. Later, my cousin advised me to always print my return ticket — just in case!

items.q: The officer asked Clara where she was from.
items.why: She asked her where she had flown from.

items.q: Clara was planning to stay for three weeks.
The officer asked if Clara had a return ticket.
Clara's cousin works in a hotel.
items.why: He's a nurse in a hospital.

items.q: What did the officer ask Clara to do at the end?
items.a: She asked her to look at the camera (and told her not to move).

items.q: Write the officer's first two questions in direct speech.
items.a: “Where have you flown from? / Where did you fly from?” · “How long are you planning to stay in Canada?”

items.q: What did Clara's cousin advise her to do?
items.a: He advised her to always print her return ticket.

exercises.title: Ahora escribe tú
exercises.es: Cuenta situaciones reales. Usa preguntas indirectas, órdenes y reporting verbs.

items.q: Recuerda una entrevista, un examen oral o una visita al médico. Escribe 3 preguntas que te hicieron: They asked me…
items.a: Ej.: They asked me why I wanted the job. They asked me if I had worked in a team before. They wanted to know when I could start.

items.q: Escribe 2 órdenes o consejos que te daban tus padres: My parents told me (not) to…
items.a: Ej.: My parents told me not to talk to strangers. They always reminded me to brush my teeth.

items.q: Cuenta un favor que alguien te pidió: … asked me to…
items.a: Ej.: My neighbour asked me to water her plants while she was on holiday.

items.q: Usa 3 reporting verbs (offer, refuse, suggest, apologise…) para contar un plan con amigos que salió mal.
items.a: Ej.: Marta suggested going to the beach, but Leo refused to go because it was cold. In the end, he apologised for being so negative and offered to drive.

checklist.es: Hago preguntas indirectas con orden de afirmativa: She asked where I lived.
checklist.en: I can report questions with statement word order.

checklist.es: Uso if / whether en las preguntas de sí / no.
checklist.en: I can use if / whether for yes / no questions.

checklist.es: Cuento órdenes con told sb (not) to y peticiones con asked sb (not) to.
checklist.en: I can report commands and requests.

checklist.es: Uso reporting verbs con su patrón: offer to, advise sb to, suggest -ing…
checklist.en: I can use reporting verbs with the right pattern.

checklist.es: Nunca digo <s>suggested me to</s> ni <s>asked me where did I live</s>.
Sigo aplicando el paso atrás y los cambios de pronombres.
checklist.en: I still backshift tenses and change pronouns.
